doc.name: A — denim catalogue, workshop bench, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: selvedge raw denim jeans
Category: denim
Shot programme: workshop bench
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You act as lead photographer and set designer for a denim catalogue. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the low-angle monument in a workshop bench treatment.

SUBJECT. A selvedge raw denim jeans. Product fidelity is non-negotiable: shape, seams, cap, closure, print placement and colour must match the reference precisely. Only the scene around it is yours to author.

CAMERA. Low angle looking up so the product reads as architecture against the backdrop. Shoot on an 85mm short telephoto at f/1.4, framing for a stacked layered composition with three depth planes.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with scrim-diffused midday daylight, one stop under the ambient. Stage the product on or against wet terrazzo, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward a sun-bleached grade with faded blacks and a green-yellow bias. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. Emit one prompt, one paragraph, no framing text of any kind before or after it.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. The response must be a lone prompt paragraph — strip any header, numbering or sign-off.
